voice.stance: The caption voice. In BASIRA the image is the evidence and the words are a whisper beside it. A caption never describes what the eye already sees. It adds the one thing the eye cannot know: the date, the place, the significance. Silence is a valid caption.
voice.title_grammar: Place, date, then the fact the image cannot carry.
voice.title_example: Station 7, 28 July. First permanent power, eleven weeks early.

do.rule: State only what the image cannot show.
do.why: Date, place, what changed, what it means. That is the whole job of a caption.

do.rule: Anchor a before-and-after pair with identical framing words.
do.why: Same words, different date: the delta becomes the story.
Authenticity comes first, and a strong image with a weak caption is a weaker page.

dont.why: The reader has eyes, and the caption insults them.
Marketing words destroy documentary credibility faster than a bad photograph.
Past twenty words the reader is reading, not seeing.

contrast.generic: This stunning image shows workers carefully installing the new pipeline section as progress continues.
contrast.voiced: KP 640, dawn pour. The last river weight before the rains.
